title: Leo inference scrapbook
body:
Top-of-page quick log (brain dump)
- trying to consolidate small experiments into one coherent notebook instead of 5 random gists.
- focus: 13B family (Llama-2 / open weights), 4-bit PTQ vs 3-bit PTQ, and a small QAT sweep for a dev branch.
- immediate goal: get a 4-bit config that keeps the hallucination / instruction-following delta < 3% on our benchmark set while reducing memory by ~2.5x.

Experiment timeline notes
- 2026-03-10: baseline fullfloat run on llama-13b-hf with default token cache and batch=1. Latency ~38 ms/token (p50), mem ~28GB. Eval (instr-follow suite, 120 prompts): pass-rate ~87%.
- 2026-03-11: PTQ 4-bit (nf4, per-channel) with our quantize.py (repo PR 842). Memory ~12GB, p50 latency ~45 ms/token (increase due to dequant overhead), pass-rate measured 85% (quick run). Observed a consistent failure mode on Q2 matrices in feed-forward for long-context prompts.
- 2026-03-12: PTQ 3-bit (custom calibration set: 5k tokens across prompts + code samples). Memory ~9GB, p50 latency ~52 ms/token, pass-rate dropped to ~79% (regressions concentrated on multi-step reasoning).

Quick prompts (dev set, use for A/B)
- P1: "You are an assistant that answers in short bullet points. Explain covariance in 3 bullets."
- P2: "Summarize the following meeting notes: <long text>. Keep to 4 sentences."
- P3: "Step-by-step solve: If I have two lists..." (used to stress chain-of-thought)
- P-code: "Implement a python function to compute top-k tokens using efficient sampling (no third-party libs)."

Notes on eval harness
- harness: eval/run_eval.py (local). Uses rouge-l, exact-match, and a simple hallucination detector (heuristic). Hard to compare across quantized runs because tokenization length > 1024 sometimes gets truncated. Add padding guard.
- quick command: python -m eval.run_eval --model ./checkpoints/llama-13b-4bit --prompts prompts/devset.json --out out/4bit-run.json
- remember to set EVAL_SEED=42 for repeatability.

Quantization detail + findings
- PTQ cfg tried: nf4 per-channel symmetric, clip_percentile=99.5, clip_by_abs=False. Calibration batches = 256 (batch size 2 seq len 512).
- QAT attempt (toy): fine-tune for 1 epoch with fake-quant hooks on attention and FFN only. Learning rate 1e-5 small; observed stability but tiny quality gains vs PTQ for reasoning tasks. Costly and slower to iterate.
- Observed numerical instability in softmax in attention when scales differ > 1e4 across heads after quant. Need to clamp pre-softmax to [-50,50] in the runtime for PTQ models. Patch idea: small per-head scale smoothing (alpha=0.01) before softmax.

Runtime flags that matter (serving-runtime local)
- --kv-cache: on/off (on speeds repeated prefixes). PTQ models show slightly higher kv-cache miss penalty (dequant cost).
- batching: continuous batching helps throughput but hurts p50 for single requests. For conversational agent, keep batching disabled for p50-sensitive routes.
- kernel selection: try kernel_combo=auto vs kernel_combo=fast-matmul (fast gives 10% better p50 on 13B-4bit but spikes for seq>2048)

Quick eval table (coarse, round numbers)
- float32 (base): mem 28GB, p50 38ms, pass 87%
- 4-bit PTQ (nf4): mem 12GB, p50 45ms, pass 85%
- 3-bit PTQ: mem 9GB, p50 52ms, pass 79%
- 4-bit QAT (toy): mem 12GB, p50 48ms, pass 86% but trained cost high

Regression trace (interesting failures)
- prompt P3 (multi-step): Q3 & Q4 heads lose step coherence. Example behavior: model repeats step 1, skips step 2, gives wrong intermediate. Suspect FFN quant noise accumulation.
- prompt P-code: 3-bit often introduces small syntactic errors in code (off-by-one index). Good signal for prompt-sensitive use-cases.

Notes-to-self: hacks to try next
- Try per-channel clip_percentile=99.9 on FFN only, keep attn at 99.5. Hypothesis: FFN has heavier tails, clipping helps without touching attention distribution.
- Add a micro-batch for calibration that includes long-context code snippets (we saw worst regressions there).
- Implement tiny QAT pass that only trains layernorm/FFN biases (freeze rest) for 2 epochs on instruction-following data (cheap).
- Add an eval metric that approximates factuality: check named-entity hallucinations via fuzzy-match to ground-truth facts.

Debug / CLI snippets
- quantize: python tools/quantize.py --input checkpoints/llama-13b/ --out checkpoints/llama-13b-nf4 --bits 4 --scheme nf4 --calib-batches 256
- run server locally: RUNTIME_ENV=local python -m runtime.serve --model checkpoints/llama-13b-nf4 --port 5100 --max-seq 2048
- fast-profile: perf/profile.py --target http://localhost:5100/generate --concurrency 8 --seq 512 --duration 120s

Open questions (for team sync)
- Is the perf regression p50 -> p50+7ms acceptable for our entry-tier hosted plans if cost halves? (bring this to product)
- Do we want to ship an automatic fallback to float32 for long reasoning prompts? Implementation complexity vs UX tradeoff.
- Should we add a quantization flag in the Redwood Console to label models as "quantized: likely regressions" for customer transparency?

Small TODO list (today)
- [ ] run 4-bit nf4 with clip_percentile=99.9 on FFN only (Samir can start)
- [ ] add padding guard to eval harness to avoid truncation mismatch (Maya)
- [ ] open a small RFC on per-head softmax clamp in runtime (me)
- [ ] push perf profile results to PR 842 and update description with numbers

Random logs / error snippets (for search)
- OOM trace when batch=2 seq=4096: "CUDA out of memory while allocating 1073741824 bytes" -> temporary workaround: set max-seq 3072 for 4-bit runs.
- Softmax NaN seen once in 3-bit run (rare): trace points to attention scaling step, likely underflow -> clamping prevented it in later runs.

Notes about prompts (meta)
- keep short prompts for throughput tests; long prompts for regressions. Label prompt files: prompts/devset.short.json and prompts/devset.long.json
- add a tag per prompt: stress/type e.g., [reasoning, code, summarization, persona] so we can slice results quickly.

End-of-scratch: quick ideas to capture for later
- explore hybrid routes: route short user queries to 3-bit for cost advantage, route long chain-of-thought to float32/dedicated pools automatically (needs routing policy work).
- keep calibration dataset in repo under data/calib/2026-03-10/ with sampling weights.

If I forget: ping Maya in #applied-ml with "quick quant update" and attach out/4bit-run.json.

-- Leo
